cascadingCourse.label: Data Visualization and Communication
cascadingCourse.description: Once a researcher or a practitioner has completed the analyses of their data, they may assume that it is a simple process to communicate their findings to relevant stakeholders, but this is almost always an incorrect assumption. Proper data communication and storytelling begins even before data is analyzed and there are proven strategies to better connect the story behind and from the data to relevant stakeholders, especially within the context of business practice. This course will focus on helping students better position themselves to successfully tell the persuasive story flowing from their data. We will use tools such as Tableau, Flourish, and the Social Media Macroscope to assist our data storytelling journey. Prerequisite: Restricted to Sophomores, Juniors, and Seniors.
cascadingCourse.courseSectionInformation: Prerequisite: Restricted to Sophomores, Juniors, and Seniors.

cascadingCourse.label: Introduction to Data Analytics Applications in Business
cascadingCourse.description: Introduces the role, methods, and implications of data analytics in business. Building on prior coursework on the fundamentals of analytics and related statistical analyses, this course provides students the opportunity to apply related theoretical and practical principles to a variety of business scenarios. After completing this course, students should (1) have a foundational understanding of the role of data analytics in business and (2) be able to apply this knowledge to real-world clients, business decisions, etc. This course will provide you the opportunity to develop and improve (1) written and oral communication skills in the form of interpersonal interaction, discussion, reports/presentations, etc., (2) knowledge of the use of spreadsheets, Python, and other analytics tools in performing common business analytics and decision-modeling, and (3) knowledge of data visualization software used for analytics-related exploration, hypothesis testing, and results-based organization and communication. Cases, class discussion, and other projects emphasize the importance of independent thinking, group processes, and communication for professional business practice. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.
cascadingCourse.sectionRegistrationNotes: Restricted to students with Sophomore, Junior, or Senior class standing. Not intended for Graduate - Urbana-Champaign.

cascadingCourse.label: AI in Business: Fundamentals, Applications, and the Future
cascadingCourse.description: Provides a comprehensive introduction to artificial intelligence spanning foundational machine learning through advanced applications including deep learning, generative AI, autonomous systems, and robotics. Explores AI's evolution and business applications across finance, marketing, manufacturing, supply chain, and human resources. Examines ethical, regulatory, and governance considerations including bias, privacy, and responsible implementation. Equips business professionals and technology leaders with technical understanding and strategic skills to navigate AI's transformative impact and leverage AI-driven solutions effectively.
